analysis: The PR adds a changelog fragment (changelog.d/flint-serving-speedups.md, lines 1-5) and a documentation paragraph in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines ~2336-2348). Neither contains executable code, so no trust boundary, key custody, attestation, authorization or cache-storage control changed in the supplied evidence. The documentation describes Flint constrained-decode chaining. Step N+1 is sampled using the mask from state confirmed through N-1 and is redrawn from retained logits, with penalty state and per-row RNG step restored, if step N changes state. It also describes a device mask cache keyed by constraint state (maskCacheKey) and adding RecursiveSI/flint-int4 to the automatic paged list at width 8 on M5 Pro, Max and Ultra. The actual implementation (SDK pin, FlintNativeProtocolConstraint, FlintAnswerStopConstraint, CBv2 chaining, paged width) is not in the supplied units, so the following security-relevant contracts are unverified. (1) Constraint enforcement under chaining: a token sampled with a stale mask must never be emitted or committed if the state moves, so tool-call/protocol constraints stay strict (the FlintRequestPolicy area). (2) The device mask cache must be keyed per constraint state and must not leak across requests or tenants (T-041 and T-028 style residual GPU state). A cache keyed only by constraint state holds no prompt data, which is low risk, but the implementation should be checked. (3) The retained logits for the redraw are extra residual prompt-derived data in GPU memory until the request retires (T-028). (4) Raising the flint-int4 concurrency to 8 interacts with the memory admission and DoS controls (T-010, T-029) and Flint memory admission. The claim that outputs are byte-identical is unverified. No regression is identifiable from these documentation-only changes. Deeper review of the SDK pin and Swift code in other batches is advisable, but nothing here establishes a vulnerability.
